newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran leader asks pilgrims to stage rally in Saudi.
newsitem.headline: Iran leader asks pilgrims to stage rally in Saudi.

text.p: Iran's supreme leader called on Iranian pilgrims on Thursday to hold a rally to denounce Israel and the United States at the Moslem haj pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia next month, despite a Saudi ban on political activities.
Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, quoted by state-run Tehran radio, said it was "necessary and important that Moslems express their disgust and disavowal of Islam's enemies" at the yearly haj.
He was referring to the "disavowal of infidels" rally, banned by conservative Sunni Saudi Arabia in the past years, which radical Shi'ite Iran says pilgrims should stage.
"The haj should be an opportunity to neutralise the plots of Arrogance (U.S) and Zionism (Israel)...and to expose the enemies of Islam," Khamenei was quoted as telling Iranian haj officials.
Saudi Arabia on Wednesday warned that pilgrims caught with political material would be severely punished and sent home.
About two million Moslems -- half of them from abroad -- are expected to perform the haj at Mecca and Medina, site of Islam's two holiest shrines.
Iran says Moslems have the right to air their political grievances during the pilgrimage, mainly through rallies against Israel and the United States.
Saudi Arabia says the haj is a purely religious affair and should not be politicised.
Saudi security forces clashed in 1987 with demonstrators in an Iranian-led rally in the streets of Mecca, killing about 400 people, mainly Iranians.

Iran boycotted the haj for the next three years. There has been no repeat of the bloodshed since the return of Iranian pilgrims in 1991 and their haj rallies have been low-key affairs mostly confined to the Iranian compounds.
